read_after_the_declared_comparisons.the_paired_same_history_row: Described, as declared. At the position whose input is the first fed token, with every earlier position the same to the bit, the state each merge puts out differs from the own answer's by a median 0.05 of its size at the first merge, 0.26 at the middle of the stack and 0.57 at the last merge after a fed label (29 cases) or a fed label and climb word (7); 0.10, 0.28 and 0.32 after a fed heading word (6, and the 6 with the label after it). One changed input token, the same history: this is the size of what the next row computes differently.
read_after_the_declared_comparisons.the_own_answers_beside_the_registered_re: Not predicted; read from the kept steps and the acquisition's recordings of the same thirty questions. The own answer on card 1 is the registered recording's whole text in 21 of the 30 and through the row that writes the first sign after KE_i in 27. No step of any of the 30 has the registered recording's score hash. Where the text is the same, the greatest change of a best token's score is 0.05 to 0.16 logits. So a state kept here is card 1's and is not compared with a state of the registered recordings without saying so; sign-counterexamples-replay-original was declared on this.
read_after_the_declared_comparisons.cost: recorder 1,961 s and keeping 452 s over the 30 questions (about 80 s a question); 38,717 positions kept, 25.5 GB on disk (the declaration derived 23.71 GiB); 91 GB free on root before, 66 GB after

failures_only: The first capture call (started 8:39 PM CT, refused at 8:55 PM CT once it had the card) was refused before any question: the recorder refuses a supplied end-of-generation token. Revised at 9:00 PM CT before any reading: the model writes the last token itself.

The second call (9:01 PM CT) was refused at its fourth question, after three were kept: the recorder refuses supplied text that leaves the model no token (the four texts that stopped at their limit). Revised at 9:05 PM CT: those four also leave their last token to the model. Neither revision changed a token of any text, and the three questions already kept hold none of the four.
A background command of mine reported exit 0 for the first refused call because it ended in a tail; later commands end with the capture's own status.
No case failed a check: every incoming, added and merged state and every layer exit of all 52,754 positions equalled the raw stream bit for bit before the raw stream was removed.
what_this_changes: The states of every fed continuation and every own answer of the thirty fitting questions are on disk, lossless, on one card: 78 texts, every position, all 105 merges (read with pipeline.overlap.fed_replay.states(run, case)). The three things a paired reading needs hold exactly: a replay under supplied tokens is the arithmetic of the pass that wrote the text; the history before a fed word is the own answer's to the bit; and after the fed word the text is what the model writes by itself. So a request of the form the owner settled (the own row's state plus what a corrected continuation's rows do differently) can be read from these arrays without another pass, and a difference found before the first forced row cannot exist. It decides no site and makes no target. It also fixes a caution for every later reading: the registered recordings and card 1 are two arithmetics (no score hash in common; 9 of 30 own texts differ), so groups are compared on one card.
